title: Customer Deployment 'Garden' Plan & Task Scrubbook
content:
Purpose and framing:

This is a lightweight but prescriptive project plan and running lab-notebook for the Customer XYZ proof-of-value engagement. Aim: deliver a working, low-latency inference path for the customer's document-summarization feature within a 5-week window, with clear handoff artifacts and measurable acceptance criteria. Use this doc as the single source for day-to-day ops, quick decisions, and the workshop agenda notes.

High-level objectives (what success looks like):
- Integration: callable Redwood API endpoint in customer sandbox that returns structured summaries (title, bullets, reading_time).
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 600ms per 512-token request in demo environment.
- Cost/ops: baseline token cost estimate and one concrete suggestion (batching or quant) that reduces unit cost by >=20% without regression.
- Reliability: automatic fallback to smaller model when throughput > threshold, documented in runbook.

Acceptance criteria (deliverables to mark POC complete):
1) Demo scenario: ingest 30k doc corpus, run 50 sample queries, outputs match golden prompt set (precision on summary headings >= 0.85 by manual QC).
2) Canary traffic test: synthetic load to reproduce 2x expected QPS for 15 minutes with <1% error rate.
3) Runbook: short runbook for customer's SRE with play to restore service and rollback steps for model variants.

Owner and primary contacts:
- Aisha Kaur (SE lead, owner) — aisha@redwood.ai
- Ben Rodriguez (Solutions Eng) — benr@redwood.ai
- Maya Singh (Customer Success lead) — mayas@redwood.ai
- Customer technical contact: Daniel Ng (CDT team) — daniel.ng@customerxyz.com

Week-by-week timeline (working weeks, 5-week plan):
Week 0 (pre-kick): account & infra prep, access checklist
- Tasks: ensure VPC peering request in place, KMS key exchange, API token created and scoped, example dataset location shared (GCS bucket).
- Owner: Ben
- Blockers: network TOC approval, ticket JIRA-ENG-879.

Week 1: Workshop + baseline integration
- Day 1 (workshop morning): 90m internal walkthrough, goals, and SLA review.
  - Agenda: intros (10m), architecture map (15m), demo of hosted API (20m), hands-on quickstart (40m).
  - Notes: keep the demo input size to 2–3 paragraphs to avoid confusing latency numbers.
- Day 1 (workshop afternoon): integration pairing — customer engineers pair with SEs to call API against sample corpus.
- Deliverable: first successful end-to-end run; smoke dashboards visible in Console.

Week 2: Performance tuning and dataflow
- Focus: batching, KV cache warmup, and quantization experiments on smaller model variants.
- Tasks: run three controlled A/B experiments, document token cost and latency per run.
- Deliverable: recommendation matrix (batch size vs latency vs cost).

Week 3: Reliability, routing, and fallback policies
- Focus: implement smart routing policy (primary high-quality model, fallback economy model), test failover under degraded capacity.
- Tasks: simulate region-level outage, verify automatic fallback triggers and report formatting remains stable.

Week 4: Pre-prod canary + ops handoff
- Tasks: run canary at 20% production QPS, execute restore drills, complete runbook and SLO doc.
- Deliverable: go/no-go decision checklist signed by customer and SE lead.

Week 5: Wrap, post-mortem, and next-steps proposal
- Deliverable: concise post-mortem, cost/latency tradeoff recommendation, proposal for Dedicated sizing if customer wants reserved capacity.

Roles & RACI (compact):
- Aisha: SE lead — accountable for final acceptance and demo narrative.
- Ben: infra & network setup — responsible for VPC/KMS and telemetry.
- Maya: CS / adoption — responsible for customer comms and acceptance logistics.
- Oliver: performance tuning — responsible for running quant/batch experiments.
- Customer dev (Daniel): integrator — responsible for embedding calls into their QA harness.

Daily run log template (copy into daily notes):
- Date:
- Actions taken:
- Outcome / smoke test results (latency, tokens, errors):
- Decision made (if any):
- Open blockers and owners:

Risk register (top items, brief mitigations):
- Network approval delays — mitigation: pre-approved cloud peering template, escalations via GTM contact.
- Data privacy / PII concerns — mitigation: use redacted sample dataset and confirm KMS/HSM policy; add PCA to contract if needed.
- Latency worse than expected in customer region — mitigation: run edge routing test and propose Dedicated zone colocated capacity.
- Model quality regressions when quantized — mitigation: keep golden prompt test suite and set quality gates; avoid quant below 4-bit until manual review.

Decision log (live):
- 2024-11-04: Agreed to start with the hosted API + routing policy vs immediate Dedicated spin-up. Rationale: faster time-to-first-demo. (Aisha, Customer)
- 2024-11-12: Approve batch size=8 as baseline after perf run 3. (Oliver)

Workshop detailed agenda (half-day engineering workshop template):
- 09:00 — Welcome + context (10m)
- 09:10 — Architecture map & dataflow (15m)
- 09:25 — Live API demo (20m)
- 09:50 — Break (10m)
- 10:00 — Guided integration lab (pairing) (60m)
- 11:00 — Perf instrumentation + Console walkthrough (30m)
- 11:30 — Open Q&A and next steps (30m)

Checklist for demo-ready environment (pre-demo QA):
- API token validated and scoped
- Telemetry hooks installed (latency + token cost)
- 10 representative documents uploaded
- Console dashboards pre-populated
- Fallback model variant configured

Notes to self / informal TODO (short):
- Remind customer: show cost impact of caching in the demo (use a repeated prefix to demonstrate KV hit).
- Keep one slide that explains quantization tradeoffs in plain English — customers always ask.
- Get legal to fast-track DPA addendum if we need to run on real customer PII for final acceptance.

Open questions for customer (action items to close during week 1 workshop):
1) Will they permit temporary access to a subset of production-like documents? (yes/no)
2) Expected steady-state QPS and peak QPS (numbers) — needed for Dedicated sizing suggestion.
3) Any region constraints (EU-only, APAC)?

Appendix: quick experimental matrix (copyable):
- Experiment A: model=s-redwood-3b, batch=1, quant=none -> 95p latency 480ms, cost x
- Experiment B: model=s-redwood-3b, batch=8, quant=none -> 95p latency 620ms, cost x*0.6
- Experiment C: model=s-redwood-2b, batch=8, quant=8-bit -> 95p latency 410ms, cost x*0.35

Final note: keep this doc alive during the engagement. It should be updated after each lab session and used to generate the final one-page summary we hand to the customer with go/no-go and suggested next steps.

-- Aisha
